The use of the beetles as a source of food proved to be quite useful. It gave a stable, movable food source to the spiders. This new food source allowed new Clanling groups to go out and settle. The populations within these cities swelled, as eggs were more easily delivered from city to city, Fulcrid stopped dying from starvation brought upon by poor hunts, and life spans increased from the better atmosphere and diets of the Clanling Anchor Points. The new cities away from the capital gave the spiders a greater sense of freedom and individuality, yet the cooperation necessary to run the new Anchor Points still bound them into unity. For now, the spiders were satisfied.

And now that her children got there fill, it was time for the Queen to get her. In return for being the spiders compassionate and humble mother, the Fulcrid would give a monthly gift off to their Queen. These gifts would be transported by a chosen spider on a wooden sled to the capital. These gifts would then be transported to the ports to the west, to be shipped off as trade goods. The problem was however, that these were just gifts, and in now way were sufficient or consistent enough to be considered proper taxes. Some Fulcrid would simply not do enough work to make gifts, and some would make gifts of poor quality. Some would try to do something unique or artistic or low effort, and end up making droppings no one would want to trade for. Some gifts were just worthless, and weren't at all worth trading, such as most goods in comparison to Fulcrid silk. Clearly it was time for reform to occur.

In order to make sure the Queen had loyal subjects who controlled the masses, she offered gifts of delicious foreign meats, hunted in the Forest of Brotherhood, and seasoned with Saen spices, to those who she deemed worthy. These offerings of meat made the chosen spiders grow fat and big, giving them an air of regality and authoiry such a figure would need. The process of selecting these spiders was painstaking and long, to the point where some died of old age before the plan ever saw light. What would happen with these spiders, is that they would be put in charge of a region, dictated by the Queen. These spiders would rule from the seat of an Anchor Point, which they personally govern, and can elect other Fulcrid they deem worthy under them. The job of these spiders is that on a monthly basis, they would send out groups of spiders who would inform the uniformed about there tax duties, and collect taxes from those who are informed. Said collected taxes would then be shipped off to the capital, for processing and trading.

This system would be known as the Crassus System. The regions that a chosen spider would rule over would be known as a Grand Crassus (a duchy), and their title would be Crassuczar (pronounced crass-us-czar, they are dukes). The Crassuczar can then choose who their heirs will be, and who will rule over the individual Crassuses (counties). These Crassus rulers under Grand Crassuses will be known as Crass (counts).

For now the Queen sent her chosen ones down south to rule over the Grand Crassuses listed here:

* **Grand Crassus of Oris Niger:** Capital: Harenam * **Grand Crassus of Concameratio** Capital: Cacumenus * **Grand Crassus of Utin Capitolio** Capital: Inviaton * **Grand Crassus of Sinus Vigilate** Capital: Speculamos * **Grand Crassus of Nauta Petras** Capital: Aranea Portum * **Grand Crassus of Regina Murum** Capital: Fonsimont * **Grand Crassus of Faeni Transibit** Capital: Pascunturmont * **Grand Crassus of Regni Terrarum** Capital: Reginapolis

The Queen herself claims the Grand Crassus of Regni Terrarum, and sends the others off on her way.

Meanwhile, Johbla sits in his palace on top of the Anchor Point of Aranea Portum. He looks at the Saen made map with older eyes. He murmurs to himself as he starts moving about wooden pieces to represent trade. Johbla was stressed with the problem he is dealing with. He had become so stressed, that he stopped visiting the SeaFairer brothel he used to visit, as he wanted more time to think. Finally Johbla had enough. He needed to find some way around that Hag!

For years, the Hags traders would always intercept trade coming through the Barrier Forest, on its way to the Forest of Brotherhood and Sentenza. The Hag's Thorac would then trick and bribe their way into getting the best deal for the best items, before sending the caravan off to their destinations with goods worth beetle droppings. Johbla had tried every trick he knew, and all would fail. He finally decided that he had to find someway to get ships around the Hag's sphere of influence, in order to get the best trade with his intended clientele. Johbla hired up ten Seafairer crews, eager to explore the Galewind Ocean to the south, and sent them off to find a better route. Hopefully, Johbla thought, that if he couldn't out-trade the Hag, he could outmaneuver it.
